clues: This syndrome was discovered in the late 2000s by scientists at the University of Virginia who were investigating severe allergic reactions to cetuximab, an IV cancer treatment. They found that patients with this reaction lived predominantly in the Southeast of the United States indicating regional exposure
Unlike typical food allergies that target proteins, this targets a carbohydrate molecule. Because these molecules take longer to digest, symptom onset is about 3-6 hours after eating food

We now know that this syndrome is caused by lone star tick bites that transfer the molecule into your blood causing an IgE mediated response. Subsequent reactions include hives, stomach pain, and anaphylaxis after eating red meat
The name actually comes from the Latin word for sausage, tracing back to 18th and 19th century Europe where many cases were linked to 'sausage poisoning'.
Approximately 12-36 hours after exposure, you might develop dilated pupils, diplopia, and weakness. Infants can become hypotonic and sleepy
A single pound of pure toxin causing this disease could theoretically kill the entire human population. In tiny doses, it's used to treat muscle spasms, migraines, hyperhidrosis, and facial wrinkles
In the 1950s, a strain of Streptomyces was isolated from a soil sample near the Castel del Monte, a 13th century castle in Italy. This compound was isolated from that bacterium.

Because of its distinct chemical structure, this liquid is a bright, transparent red that also turns the patient's urine red or pink. It is sometimes known as the 'Red Devil' because of this color and potent side effects
This drug stabilizes topoisomerase, stopping replication and is known for its dose-dependent cardiotoxicity
In 1909, a German physician created the first recorded version of this using a ring made of silkworm guts that was placed inside patients

Because the addition of metals was thought to make this more effective, pure silver was later wrapped around the ring, but the silver was absorbed and patients' gums turned bluish-black. This led to the use of other metals such as copper
While other strange shapes were tried like fern, snakes, and stingrays, current devices are in a T-shape and over 99% effective, lasting 3-10 years
Do you remember what the pineal gland does? This was initially isolated in 1958 from bovine pineal glands while searching for a treatment to lighten frog skin pigmentation

Mitochondria are the main producers of this substance across nearly all life forms. Its initial function was likely to fight oxidative stress and peak concentrations in the body typically appear between midnight and 8AM
Available as an over-the-counter supplement, this helps regular the sleep-wake cycle and is commonly used to help shift timing of the circadian rhythm
